queue.title: What to Check During an AC Maintenance Tune-Up: Capacitor to Drain Line

draft.title: Residential Split AC Maintenance Tune-Up Procedure
draft.summary: An HVAC technician demonstrates a complete preventive maintenance check on a split air conditioning system. The video covers electrical testing, non-invasive system diagnostics, drain line cleaning, and indoor unit inspection.
draft.safety: Always disconnect main electrical power and properly discharge capacitors before handling electrical components.
steps: Check compressor and fan motor amperage using a clamp meter
Disconnect power and test the run capacitor's capacitance and power factor
Clear the outdoor condensate drain line using a wet-dry vacuum
Check system operating parameters non-invasively using digital gauges and app
Inspect and clean the indoor evaporator coil and drain pan
Flush and prime the condensate drain line with clean water
draft.subject: Preventive Maintenance

review.reason: Practical step-by-step demonstration of AC maintenance covering both electrical and airflow diagnostics.

queue.title: Why and How to Test Heat Pump Defrost - Short #310

draft.title: Heat Pump Defrost System Overview and Testing
draft.summary: Explains why heat pumps require defrost cycles and outlines key principles for testing defrost controls and sensors. Discusses differences between time-temperature and demand defrost logic.
draft.safety: Always disconnect electrical power before servicing or inspecting internal wiring on the outdoor unit.
steps: Identify whether the defrost system uses time-temperature or demand logic.
Determine if sensors are snap-action switches or variable-resistance thermistors.
Consult manufacturer guidelines before initiating a forced defrost test.
Observe reversing valve operation, outdoor fan shutoff, and supplemental heat activation.
Verify that temperature sensors are physically attached to the coil properly.
Inspect outdoor unit for ice accumulation, blocked airflow, or drainage issues.
draft.subject: Refrigerant & Diagnostics

review.reason: The content contains valuable theoretical information, but the video is an audio podcast with a static logo image.

queue.title: Prepping and tiling a shower. Start to finish. #tile #howtotile

draft.title: Installing Backer Board and Waterproofing a Shower
draft.summary: This video demonstrates the step-by-step process of preparing a shower for tiling, including installing backer board, waterproofing, building a shower pan, and laying tile.
draft.safety: Wear appropriate personal protective equipment, including safety glasses and gloves, when handling power tools and building materials.
steps: Measure and install shower backer board to the wall studs.
Cut and fit PVC pipes for the shower drain system.
Mix and apply mud bed mix for the shower floor.
Install waterproofing sheet membrane and sealant.
Apply thin-set mortar and lay wall and floor tiles.
draft.subject: Tile Installation

review.reason: This video provides a comprehensive, detailed guide on shower preparation and tiling suitable for advanced civil maintenance technicians.

draft.title: Installing a Floating Shower Bench Seat
draft.summary: This video demonstrates how to build and install a floating bench seat inside a shower using foam board and sealant.
draft.safety: Ensure proper ventilation and wear safety glasses when operating power tools and handling sealants.
steps: Measure and mark the shower wall for bench height.
Cut foam board to the correct dimensions using a saw.
Apply sealant along the marked wall lines.
Press and secure the foam board bench into place.
Flood test the shower floor to check for leaks.
draft.subject: Tile Installation

review.reason: This video provides a clear and practical demonstration of installing a floating shower bench seat.

queue.title: Panel Wiring is NOT for Everyone

draft.title: Kitchen Fan Control Panel Troubleshooting and Repair
draft.summary: Demonstrates how to troubleshoot a commercial kitchen ventilation panel, replace a damaged contactor, repair faulty switch contacts, and wire thermal overload relays.
draft.safety: Ensure the power supply is completely isolated before touching internal panel components or changing contact blocks.
steps: Inspect control panel components for thermal damage or burnt contacts.
Replace damaged contactors with correctly rated replacement parts.
Check auxiliary switch contact blocks for physical fractures or loose mechanisms.
Transfer wiring to an available working contact pair on the switch assembly.
Verify thermal overload relay NC 95-96 and NO 97-98 terminal functions.
draft.subject: Motor Control

review.reason: Clear real-world explanation of troubleshooting motor control circuits and thermal overload terminals.
unsafe: Operating inside an open live panel without electrical safety gloves
